script: They capped pre‑med loans, but my teaching major got a death sentence.. I heard someone say we need loan caps that actually match the field you're going into. Like, seriously, if you're in teaching or social work, why should you be able to borrow the same insane amount as a pre‑med or engineer? (I mean, the audacity of that, right?) They argued that if a major leads to a low‑pay job, the cap should be lower to protect people. Imagine you're 18, eyes on a fancy school, but the tuition is a whole other world away from what you'll earn in a decade. The point is: you can't be expected to calculate that debt spiral when you're still figuring out your favorite meme. If the school you dream of costs more than you realistically can afford, you don't need to go there. The whole "four years are everything" vibe is a myth. In a life lived right, you just go to school, get a degree, and start making moves. (Literally insane, right?) So yeah, caps that match the future paycheck make sense. If you're studying a field that pays less, you shouldn't have to take on a debt that'll haunt you for 18 years. And if you're aiming for a dream school, you should know if it's even on your radar before you sign that loan paperwork. (Honestly, that's the tea.)
